title: Sufficient statistic as a named data compression
dek: T(y) is sufficient if the conditional law of the data given T does not depend on θ. Wikipedia definition. Exponential families make T obvious.
story: A statistic T(y) is sufficient for θ if, once you know T, the leftover details of y carry no further information about θ. Fisher's factorization theorem is the working test: f(y|θ)=g(T(y),θ)h(y).
Exponential families hand you T for free. That is why the expfam plates keep saying 'the list of counts disappeared except as a sum'.

Ancillarity and completeness are neighbouring encyclopedia words this studio will not turn into a qualifying exam. We need the compression slogan for GLMs and for 'why the MLE depends on y only through …'.
deepTitle: Compression versus throwing away the design
deep: Sufficiency is relative to a model. If the model is wrong, T may be insufficient for the truth.
The whole sample is always sufficient; the point is reduction.
In a Cox model, the partial likelihood uses risk-set structure, not a single Poisson T.
Do not confuse sufficient statistics with p-values.

visual.caption: Data in, T extracted, likelihood depends on y only through T. The leftover h(y) does not see θ.
